question: If the compound interest on a certain sum of 2 years at 4% per annum is ₹1530. What would be the simple interest on the same sum for the same period and at the same rate?
solution:
**Given:**

C.I = Rs. 1530

Rate = 4%

Time = 2 years

**Concept used:**

C.I = P[(1 + R/100)T - 1]

S.I = (P × T × R)/100

Here, P = sum, T = time, R = rate

**Calculation:**

Let the sum be Rs. P

Now, 1530 = P[(1 + 4/100)² - 1]

⇒ 1530 = P[(1 + 1/25)² - 1]

⇒ 1530 = P[(26/25)² - 1]

⇒ 1530 = P[(676/625) - 1]

⇒ 1530 = P[(51/625]

⇒ P = 1530 × (625/51)

⇒ P = 18750

S.I = [(18750 × 2 × 4)/100]

⇒ 150000/100 = 1500

**∴ The simple interest on the same sum for the same period and at the same rate is ₹1500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Calculation:**

Here, 4% = 1/25

Let Principle be 625 units

Interest for 1st year = 625 × 1/25 = 25 units

Interest for 2nd year = 625 × 1/25 + 25 × 1/25

⇒ 25 + 1 = 26 units

Total C.I. = 25 + 26 = 51 units

⇒ 51 units = 1530 

⇒ 625 units = 18750

Now, the S.I. for 2 years at 4% on P = 18750

⇒ (18750 × 2 × 4)/100 = Rs. 1,500

H**ence, The simple interest is Rs.1500**
